chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When a man commits adultery with his father's wife or his father's slave girl, that does not prohibit her from her husband, nor does it prohibit the slave girl from her master. That prohibition from him occurs only when he has intercourse with the slave girl while she is lawful (to him), so that slave girl becomes permanently unlawful to his son and to his father. And when a man marries a woman with a lawful marriage, that woman becomes unlawful to his father and to his son.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father and son marrying the same woman if the man commits adultery with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between prohibitions arising from marriage (which are permanent for the father and son) and those from adultery, clarifying that a man's illicit act with his father's wife does not bar the father from remarrying her. It further establishes the principle of 'permanent prohibition' (haram al-tasrī) for a slave girl if the man has sexual relations with her while she is still lawful to him, a nuance significant in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of concubines. The ruling underscores the distinct legal mechanisms of 'marriage' versus 'possession' in creating mahram relationships within the family structure.
